data.cultural_impact: The name Shaddam holds historical significance as it was the name of the legendary ruler of the ancient Mesopotamian city of Babylon, King Hammurabi, whose famous code of laws is admired in the Islamic world for its fairness and justice. This name evokes a sense of power and authority, which is a desirable aspect in a leader in many Islamic cultures. It also carries a strong connection to the rich heritage of Mesopotamia, which is an essential part of Islamic history and identity.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic context, the name Shaddad (a variant of Shaddam) is mentioned in the Quran as one of the names of Allah (SWT), signifying His absolute power and control over all things. The name is also mentioned in several Hadith where it refers to a high-ranking angel in charge of the Throne). Therefore, the name Shaddam carries a spiritual significance of submission to Allah's will and recognition of His sovereignty and power. It is a reminder of the prayer, "Allahumma j'alna qawanan fil-Qaul," which means, "O Allah, make us masters in Your religion."

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Shaddad ibn Aws was the father of Marhab, who was one of the ten champions sent by the Prophet Muhammad to meet the Byzantine and Persian armies at the Battle of Mu'tah in 629 AD.
Shaddad ibn Hammad was a legendary king of the pre-Islamic Arabs of the Ghassanid tribe who ruled over the region of Homs in Syria. He is known for his wealth, generosity, and military prowess.

trends: Sci-fi name for a planet in Dune novel by Frank Herbert
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Shaddam is most commonly associated with Saddam Hussein, the former Iraqi dictator. His name gained international notoriety during the Gulf War in the 1990s. In modern times, Shaddam is also recognized as the name of the ruling Emperor in the Dune science fiction novel by Frank Herbert. This dual significance has led to Shaddam being used in various contexts, including pop culture references, historical analysis, and literary interpretation.
